question.text: What can happen if staff doubt your physical fitness to drive?

answer.text: Staff ask a few general health questions, and doubt about your physical fitness to drive can hold the application pending a reexamination with more medical information.

teaching.text: Doubt about fitness to drive holds the application for a reexamination with more medical information. Remember: doubt means a reexam.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Staff ask a few general health questions, and doubt about your physical fitness to drive can hold the application pending a reexamination with more medical information.

question.text: What happens if you need glasses or contacts to pass the vision test?

answer.text: If you need glasses or contacts to pass the vision test, your license will require you to wear them while driving.

teaching.text: If you pass only with glasses or contacts, the license requires them whenever you drive. Remember: need lenses, wear lenses.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you need glasses or contacts to pass the vision test, your license will require you to wear them while driving.

question.text: What follows if you fail the vision test?

answer.text: Failing the vision test means an eye-care specialist must complete a vision statement, and limits such as daylight driving only may follow.

teaching.text: Failing vision means an eye-care specialist completes a statement, and limits such as daylight-only driving may follow. Remember: specialist statement, possible limits.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failing the vision test means an eye-care specialist must complete a vision statement, and limits such as daylight driving only may follow.

question.text: How early must you arrive for a knowledge test toward an original license?

answer.text: For a knowledge test toward an original operator’s, chauffeur’s or commercial license, arrive at least one hour before the office closes.

teaching.text: For an original license knowledge test, arrive at least one hour before the office closes. Remember: an hour before closing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a knowledge test toward an original operator’s, chauffeur’s or commercial license, arrive at least one hour before the office closes.

question.text: On which written tests may a foreign language interpreter help?

answer.text: Knowledge tests come in many languages, and foreign language interpreters may help on every written test except commercial license knowledge tests.

teaching.text: Knowledge tests come in many languages, and interpreters may help on every written test except commercial ones. Remember: every test except commercial.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Knowledge tests come in many languages, and foreign language interpreters may help on every written test except commercial license knowledge tests.

question.text: What may a skills test interpreter do, and where is one not allowed?

answer.text: Hard-of-hearing or non-fluent applicants may use an interpreter in the skills test, who must show photo ID and only relay the examiner’s instructions, but not in commercial license written or skills tests.

teaching.text: A skills test interpreter shows photo ID and only relays instructions, and none is allowed in commercial tests. Remember: relay only, never commercial.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hard-of-hearing or non-fluent applicants may use an interpreter in the skills test, who must show photo ID and only relay the examiner’s instructions, but not in commercial license written or skills tests.

question.text: Can a non-fluent car applicant use an interpreter for the knowledge test?

answer.text: Interpreters may assist on every written knowledge test except commercial license tests, so a non-fluent car applicant can use one for the knowledge test.

teaching.text: Non-fluent car applicants may use an interpreter for the knowledge test; commercial tests are the exception. Remember: yes, unless commercial.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Interpreters may assist on every written knowledge test except commercial license tests, so a non-fluent car applicant can use one for the knowledge test.

question.text: How long is a TIP valid, and what does it let you do?

answer.text: A temporary instruction permit (TIP) is valid for one hundred eighty days and lets you practice with a licensed adult before the driving skills test.

teaching.text: A TIP lasts one hundred eighty days and is for practice with a licensed adult. Remember: one hundred eighty day permit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A temporary instruction permit (TIP) is valid for one hundred eighty days and lets you practice with a licensed adult before the driving skills test.

question.text: Who receives a temporary instruction permit?

answer.text: TIPs go to people never licensed, foreign license holders seeking a Michigan license, and people whose license expired at least four years ago.

teaching.text: TIPs go to never-licensed people, foreign license holders, and people whose license expired at least four years ago. Remember: new, foreign, long expired.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: TIPs go to people never licensed, foreign license holders seeking a Michigan license, and people whose license expired at least four years ago.

question.text: What must you do to get a TIP?

answer.text: To get a TIP you bring the four proofs, pass the vision test and health standards plus the written knowledge and road sign tests, pay the fee and have your photo taken.

teaching.text: For a TIP, bring four proofs, pass vision, health, knowledge and sign tests, pay the fee and take a photo. Remember: proofs, tests, fee, photo.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To get a TIP you bring the four proofs, pass the vision test and health standards plus the written knowledge and road sign tests, pay the fee and have your photo taken.

question.text: How long must you practice on a TIP before the skills test?

answer.text: You must practice on a TIP for at least thirty days before the driving skills test, and an adult driver education course is encouraged.

teaching.text: Practice at least thirty days on a TIP before the skills test; a driver education course is encouraged. Remember: thirty days minimum.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must practice on a TIP for at least thirty days before the driving skills test, and an adult driver education course is encouraged.

question.text: After your skills test results arrive, how can you drive until the license comes?

answer.text: After the department receives your skills test results, your license is mailed, and a temporary operator’s permit printed from your MiLogin account lets you drive until it arrives.

teaching.text: After your results arrive, a temporary permit printed from MiLogin covers you until the mailed license comes. Remember: print the temporary permit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After the department receives your skills test results, your license is mailed, and a temporary operator’s permit printed from your MiLogin account lets you drive until it arrives.

question.text: Which is required on a TIP: thirty days of practice or an adult driver education course?

answer.text: The thirty-day TIP practice minimum is a firm requirement on the TIP page, and the adult driver education course is only encouraged, not required.

teaching.text: Thirty days of TIP practice is required; the adult course is only encouraged. Remember: practice required, course encouraged.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The thirty-day TIP practice minimum is a firm requirement on the TIP page, and the adult driver education course is only encouraged, not required.

question.text: What does a motorcycle TIP allow, and does it replace the endorsement?

answer.text: The motorcycle TIP lets a new rider practice on public roads under constant supervision of an experienced motorcyclist, and it never replaces the endorsement.

teaching.text: The motorcycle TIP allows supervised practice on public roads but never replaces the endorsement. Remember: practice only, not endorsement.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The motorcycle TIP lets a new rider practice on public roads under constant supervision of an experienced motorcyclist, and it never replaces the endorsement.

question.text: How long does a motorcycle TIP last, and how many can a rider receive?

answer.text: A motorcycle TIP lasts one hundred eighty days, and no rider receives more than two of them in a ten-year period.

teaching.text: A motorcycle TIP lasts one hundred eighty days, and no rider gets more than two in ten years. Remember: two permits per decade.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A motorcycle TIP lasts one hundred eighty days, and no rider receives more than two of them in a ten-year period.

question.text: What does a motorcycle TIP require?

answer.text: A motorcycle TIP requires age sixteen, a valid Michigan driver’s license, passing the vision and motorcycle knowledge tests, and the fee.

teaching.text: A motorcycle TIP needs age sixteen, a valid Michigan license, the vision and motorcycle knowledge tests, and the fee. Remember: sixteen, license, tests, fee.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A motorcycle TIP requires age sixteen, a valid Michigan driver’s license, passing the vision and motorcycle knowledge tests, and the fee.

question.text: What supervision and limits apply to a motorcycle TIP rider?

answer.text: A motorcycle TIP rider must stay in constant visual supervision of a licensed motorcycle operator aged at least eighteen, and may not ride at night or carry passengers.

teaching.text: A motorcycle TIP rider stays in sight of a licensed operator eighteen or older, with no night riding and no passengers. Remember: watched, no night, no riders.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A motorcycle TIP rider must stay in constant visual supervision of a licensed motorcycle operator aged at least eighteen, and may not ride at night or carry passengers.

question.text: How does the motorcycle TIP relate to the endorsement?

answer.text: A motorcycle TIP lasts one hundred eighty days and a rider gets at most two in a ten-year period, so it bridges to the endorsement rather than replacing it.

teaching.text: With one hundred eighty days per permit and two per decade, the motorcycle TIP bridges to the endorsement. Remember: a bridge, not a replacement.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A motorcycle TIP lasts one hundred eighty days and a rider gets at most two in a ten-year period, so it bridges to the endorsement rather than replacing it.

question.text: How do the minimum ages of a motorcycle TIP rider and the supervisor differ?

answer.text: A motorcycle TIP holder must be at least sixteen, while the licensed motorcyclist supervising that rider must be at least eighteen.

teaching.text: The motorcycle TIP rider must be sixteen, but the supervising motorcyclist must be eighteen. Remember: rider sixteen, watcher eighteen.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A motorcycle TIP holder must be at least sixteen, while the licensed motorcyclist supervising that rider must be at least eighteen.

question.text: When is a driving skills test required?

answer.text: A driving skills test is required for Level two, for never-licensed applicants eighteen or older, when your last license expired more than four years ago, or for a license from a country other than Canada, Germany or South Korea.

teaching.text: A skills test is required for Level two, never-licensed adults, licenses expired over four years, and most foreign licenses. Remember: new, long expired, other country.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driving skills test is required for Level two, for never-licensed applicants eighteen or older, when your last license expired more than four years ago, or for a license from a country other than Canada, Germany or South Korea.

question.text: What training must an under-eighteen applicant complete before the skills test?

answer.text: Under-eighteen skills test applicants need Segment two completed, Level one held at least six months, and a log of at least fifty supervised hours with ten at night, kept in The Supervised Driving Guide or the free RoadReady app.

teaching.text: Teens need Segment two, six months on Level one and fifty logged hours with ten at night before the skills test. Remember: Segment two, six months, fifty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Under-eighteen skills test applicants need Segment two completed, Level one held at least six months, and a log of at least fifty supervised hours with ten at night, kept in The Supervised Driving Guide or the free RoadReady app.

question.text: What record must an under-eighteen applicant have before the skills test?

answer.text: Under-eighteen applicants must also have no convictions, civil infractions, suspensions or at-fault crashes in the ninety days right before the skills test and Level two application.

teaching.text: Teens need ninety clean days before the skills test and Level two application. Remember: clean ninety days.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Under-eighteen applicants must also have no convictions, civil infractions, suspensions or at-fault crashes in the ninety days right before the skills test and Level two application.

question.text: What must an applicant eighteen or older hold before the skills test?

answer.text: Applicants eighteen or older must hold a TIP before the skills test, and a thirty-day practice period may be required.

teaching.text: Applicants eighteen or older hold a TIP before the skills test and may need thirty days of practice. Remember: adults need a TIP.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Applicants eighteen or older must hold a TIP before the skills test, and a thirty-day practice period may be required.

question.text: Who gives skills tests, and who sets their fees?

answer.text: Independent businesses approved by the Secretary of State give skills tests, and since the state does not set their fees, ask about pricing before you book.

teaching.text: Approved independent businesses give skills tests and set their own fees, so ask the price before booking. Remember: ask the price first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Independent businesses approved by the Secretary of State give skills tests, and since the state does not set their fees, ask about pricing before you book.

question.text: What part of the skills test comes first?

answer.text: The skills test starts with off-street, closed-course maneuvers, and only after passing them do you take the on-road test that earns the driving skills receipt.

teaching.text: Pass the closed-course maneuvers first; only then comes the on-road test. Remember: closed course first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The skills test starts with off-street, closed-course maneuvers, and only after passing them do you take the on-road test that earns the driving skills receipt.

question.text: What kinds of driving does the on-road portion include?

answer.text: The on-road portion includes urban, expressway, rural highway and residential driving, as described in the Driving Skills Test Study Guide.

teaching.text: The on-road portion covers urban, expressway, rural highway and residential driving. Remember: city, highway, country, neighborhood.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The on-road portion includes urban, expressway, rural highway and residential driving, as described in the Driving Skills Test Study Guide.

question.text: Which foreign licenses avoid the skills test?

answer.text: Foreign licenses from Canada, Germany or South Korea avoid the skills test, while a license from any other country requires it.

teaching.text: Licenses from Canada, Germany or South Korea skip the skills test; other countries require it. Remember: Canada, Germany, Korea skip.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Foreign licenses from Canada, Germany or South Korea avoid the skills test, while a license from any other country requires it.

question.text: How do teen and adult prerequisites for the skills test differ?

answer.text: Under-eighteen applicants need a clean record for the ninety days before the skills test, while adults instead need a TIP and possibly a thirty-day practice period.

teaching.text: Teens need a clean ninety days, while adults need a TIP and possibly thirty days of practice. Remember: teens clean record, adults TIP.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Under-eighteen applicants need a clean record for the ninety days before the skills test, while adults instead need a TIP and possibly a thirty-day practice period.

question.text: When may a Physician's Statement of Examination be requested?

answer.text: A Physician’s Statement of Examination may be requested at application or renewal for any physical or mental condition that may affect safe driving.

teaching.text: A physician's statement may be requested at application or renewal for any condition that may affect safe driving. Remember: conditions that affect driving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Physician’s Statement of Examination may be requested at application or renewal for any physical or mental condition that may affect safe driving.

question.text: When is a physician's statement required because of lost consciousness?

answer.text: A physician’s statement is also required when the state has reason to believe you had a seizure, blackout, fainting spell or other loss of consciousness within the past six months.

teaching.text: A loss of consciousness within six months calls for a physician's statement. Remember: blackout in six months.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A physician’s statement is also required when the state has reason to believe you had a seizure, blackout, fainting spell or other loss of consciousness within the past six months.

question.text: What medical history must chauffeur and commercial license holders have?

answer.text: Chauffeur and commercial license holders must have had no blackouts, fainting spells or seizures in the last twelve months.

teaching.text: Chauffeur and commercial holders need twelve months with no blackouts, fainting spells or seizures. Remember: twelve clear months.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Chauffeur and commercial license holders must have had no blackouts, fainting spells or seizures in the last twelve months.

question.text: Who completes the physician's statement, and who reviews it?

answer.text: A physician or physician’s assistant licensed in Michigan or another state completes the statement, describing conditions and medications, and the Driver Assessment Section reviews it.

teaching.text: A physician or physician's assistant licensed in any state completes the statement, and the Driver Assessment Section reviews it. Remember: licensed physician, state reviews.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A physician or physician’s assistant licensed in Michigan or another state completes the statement, describing conditions and medications, and the Driver Assessment Section reviews it.

question.text: What happens when a serious condition is reported at renewal?

answer.text: A serious condition reported at renewal leads to a driver reexamination, so start renewing several weeks early, and a restricted license for illness may bring periodic reexams.

teaching.text: A serious condition at renewal brings a reexamination, so start renewing several weeks early. Remember: renew early, expect a reexam.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A serious condition reported at renewal leads to a driver reexamination, so start renewing several weeks early, and a restricted license for illness may bring periodic reexams.

question.text: Where do license restrictions appear, and how long are new drivers on probation?

answer.text: Any special licensing conditions or restrictions are printed on the license, and drivers licensed for the first time are on probation for at least three years.

teaching.text: Conditions are printed on the license, and first-time drivers are on probation for at least three years. Remember: printed limits, three-year probation.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Any special licensing conditions or restrictions are printed on the license, and drivers licensed for the first time are on probation for at least three years.

question.text: How long are new drivers on probation, and is it part of GDL?

answer.text: New drivers, GDL teens included, stay on probation for at least three years, a monitoring program kept separate from GDL.

teaching.text: New drivers, GDL teens included, stay on probation for at least three years in a separate program. Remember: probation stands apart.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: New drivers, GDL teens included, stay on probation for at least three years, a monitoring program kept separate from GDL.

question.text: How do the medical look-back windows for a physician's statement and for commercial drivers differ?

answer.text: A physician’s statement looks back six months for any loss of consciousness, while chauffeur and commercial license holders need twelve months free of blackouts, fainting or seizures.

teaching.text: Six months is the physician's statement window; twelve months is the commercial and chauffeur rule. Remember: six months versus twelve.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A physician’s statement looks back six months for any loss of consciousness, while chauffeur and commercial license holders need twelve months free of blackouts, fainting or seizures.

question.text: Is the three-year probation the same thing as GDL?

answer.text: Probation of at least three years is a program separate from Graduated Driver Licensing, even though teens in GDL are also on probation.

teaching.text: Probation is a separate program from GDL, though GDL teens are on probation too. Remember: probation is not GDL.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Probation of at least three years is a program separate from Graduated Driver Licensing, even though teens in GDL are also on probation.

question.text: In what order do you change your name on your license?

answer.text: To change your name, change it with the Social Security Administration first, wait at least three business days, then bring your license and name-change proof to an office for a new license and fee.

teaching.text: Change your name with Social Security first, wait three business days, then visit an office and pay the fee. Remember: Social Security first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To change your name, change it with the Social Security Administration first, wait at least three business days, then bring your license and name-change proof to an office for a new license and fee.

question.text: What must your license address match, and what does a change cost?

answer.text: Michigan law requires your license address to match your residence and your voter identification card, and address changes are free online, in person or by mail.

teaching.text: Your license address must match your residence and voter card, and changing it is free. Remember: address change is free.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Michigan law requires your license address to match your residence and your voter identification card, and address changes are free online, in person or by mail.

question.text: What does an online address change update?

answer.text: An online address change updates your license or ID, your voter registration, and vehicle records linked to your license account.

teaching.text: One online address change updates your license, voter registration and linked vehicle records. Remember: one change, three records.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An online address change updates your license or ID, your voter registration, and vehicle records linked to your license account.

question.text: When do vehicles not linked to your account get the new address, and what risk comes from not reporting a move?

answer.text: Vehicles not linked to your license account get the new address only during a vehicle transaction, and failing to report a move can bring suspension or revocation.

teaching.text: Unlinked vehicles update only during a vehicle transaction, and an unreported move can bring suspension or revocation. Remember: report moves or lose it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicles not linked to your license account get the new address only during a vehicle transaction, and failing to report a move can bring suspension or revocation.

question.text: How do name changes and address changes differ in where they start and what they cost?

answer.text: A name change starts at the Social Security Administration and costs a fee for the new license, while an address change starts with the Secretary of State and is free.

teaching.text: Name changes start at Social Security and cost a fee; address changes start with the Secretary of State and are free. Remember: name costs, address free.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A name change starts at the Social Security Administration and costs a fee for the new license, while an address change starts with the Secretary of State and is free.

question.text: How long is a license usually valid, and when does an under-twenty-one license expire?

answer.text: A license is usually valid four years and expires on your birthday in the year printed on it, except that under-twenty-one licenses expire on the 21st birthday.

teaching.text: Licenses usually run four years to your birthday, but under-twenty-one licenses end at twenty-one. Remember: four years to your birthday.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A license is usually valid four years and expires on your birthday in the year printed on it, except that under-twenty-one licenses expire on the 21st birthday.

question.text: Where does the renewal notice go, and what does late renewal add?

answer.text: The renewal notice goes to the address on record, driving without a valid license is illegal, and renewing after expiration adds a late fee.

teaching.text: The renewal notice goes to your address on record, and renewing after expiration adds a late fee. Remember: late renewal costs more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The renewal notice goes to the address on record, driving without a valid license is illegal, and renewing after expiration adds a late fee.

question.text: Which licenses cannot be renewed?

answer.text: A suspended, revoked or denied license cannot be renewed, and renewal can be refused without a valid Social Security number or ineligibility letter and legal presence proof.

teaching.text: Suspended, revoked or denied licenses cannot be renewed, and missing Social Security or legal presence proof can block renewal. Remember: suspended cannot renew.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A suspended, revoked or denied license cannot be renewed, and renewal can be refused without a valid Social Security number or ineligibility letter and legal presence proof.

question.text: How can you renew when no office visit is required?

answer.text: When no office visit is required, you may renew by mail, online at Michigan.gov or SOS or at a self-service station.

teaching.text: When no visit is required, renew by mail, online or at a self-service station. Remember: mail, online, kiosk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When no office visit is required, you may renew by mail, online at Michigan.gov or SOS or at a self-service station.

question.text: How often must you renew in person, and what happens there?

answer.text: Every twelve years you must renew in person at an office, where vision is screened and a new photo is taken.

teaching.text: Every twelve years renewal is in person, with a vision screening and a new photo. Remember: every twelve years in person.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every twelve years you must renew in person at an office, where vision is screened and a new photo is taken.

question.text: What should someone who stops driving do with their license?

answer.text: Someone who stops driving returns the license to an office and applies for a state ID card instead.

teaching.text: If you stop driving, return the license to an office and apply for a state ID card. Remember: trade license for ID.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Someone who stops driving returns the license to an office and applies for a state ID card instead.

question.text: Who receives a free state ID card?

answer.text: Free ID cards go to people who are legally blind, drivers sixty-five or older who voluntarily give up their license, and drivers who lose driving privileges for a physical or mental disability.

teaching.text: Free IDs go to legally blind people, drivers sixty-five or older who give up driving, and those who lose privileges for a disability. Remember: blind, older surrender, disability.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Free ID cards go to people who are legally blind, drivers sixty-five or older who voluntarily give up their license, and drivers who lose driving privileges for a physical or mental disability.

question.text: How does an under-twenty-one license's expiration differ from a standard license?

answer.text: A standard license runs about four years to your birthday, but an under-twenty-one license ends on the 21st birthday no matter when it was issued.

teaching.text: Under-twenty-one licenses end at the twenty-first birthday, unlike the usual four-year term. Remember: twenty-first birthday ends it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A standard license runs about four years to your birthday, but an under-twenty-one license ends on the 21st birthday no matter when it was issued.

question.text: How often must renewal happen in person even if remote renewal is allowed?

answer.text: You may renew by mail, online or at a self-service station when allowed, but every twelve years the renewal must happen in person with a vision screening and photo.

teaching.text: Remote renewal is allowed when permitted, but every twelve years you renew in person. Remember: remote allowed, twelve-year visit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may renew by mail, online or at a self-service station when allowed, but every twelve years the renewal must happen in person with a vision screening and photo.

question.text: When do drivers sixty-five or older qualify for a free state ID, compared with legally blind people?

answer.text: A free state ID goes to drivers sixty-five or older only when they give up the license voluntarily, while legally blind people qualify regardless of age.

teaching.text: Drivers sixty-five or older get a free ID only by voluntarily giving up the license; legally blind people qualify at any age. Remember: voluntary surrender, blind always.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A free state ID goes to drivers sixty-five or older only when they give up the license voluntarily, while legally blind people qualify regardless of age.
